source: scripts/wc2026_predictor.py + scripts/wc2026_tune_predictor.py — one entry per upgrade-adoption decision. Each entry records the upgrade audit it is based on, before/after metrics on the same graded set, the CI method, and an honest verdict. Adopted upgrades flow into the predictor; rejected ones are re-checked after more matches grade.

iterations.honest_verdict: 30K random search + 1K paired-bootstrap fine-tune found a brier_delta of -0.000375 vs the in-search parent with 95% CI [-0.001823, 0.001210] which crosses 0. real_lift=false on n=29 WC2026 actuals + 563 backtest. Baseline coefficients (K_factor=40, HOME_ADV=0.4, POISSON_B=1.6, DC_RHO=-0.08, no Heuer decay) are kept. The large negative vs_baseline_brier_delta (~-0.089) is partly an artefact of the search corpus mixing in calibrated backtest rows; the within-search CI is the honest test of additional lift on top of the existing isotonic calibrator. Re-run after MD2+ graded actuals.
iterations.commit_title_correction: Published in commit aaa38b2e under HTR-iteration title due to a stale COMMIT_EDITMSG template at commit time. The correct audit title for this iteration is: 'feat(wc2026): 30K hyperparameter search + 1K fine-tune; baseline=0.670 brier, best=0.581 brier, lift=-0.000375 (CI [-0.00182, +0.00121])'. This corrective commit carries the intended message in its body.

iterations.ci_method: paired bootstrap on per-match Brier deltas, 300 reps, percentile 2.5/97.5

implementation.fit_strategy: per-class one-vs-rest sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip', y_min=0, y_max=1), refit each predictor run on every graded WC2026 fixture resolvable via wc2026_db.actual_for, renormalised across H/D/A.
implementation.raw_probs_preserved: every calibrated prediction also carries p_home_raw / p_draw_raw / p_away_raw so the locker, UI, and audit log can recover the uncalibrated values.

iterations.honest_caveat: The 95% CI excludes 0 but n=29 is small AND the calibrator is fit IN-SAMPLE on the same fixtures the Brier is measured on, so the +0.214 brier_delta is a near-best-case in-sample fit, not an out-of-sample lift. The decision to adopt rests on (a) isotonic being the only one of the five audited upgrades whose CI strictly excluded 0 in the favourable direction, (b) raw probs being preserved so the change is fully reversible by ignoring the new keys, and (c) the calibrator refitting each predictor run so it self-corrects as new matches grade. Re-evaluate with held-out splits once n_graded >= 60.

iterations.honest_verdict: Brier delta -0.0165 favours heuer (lower is better), but 95% CI [-0.111, +0.065] straddles 0. Winner delta +3.45pp 95% CI [0.0, +10.34] touches the 0 lower bound. No statistically significant lift on n=29 graded matches — re-check after MD2+ MD3+ add graded actuals.

CI straddles 0 AND the odds in wc2026_value_bets.json are placeholder (uniform 1.91/3.70/3.80 every match because the hosting IP is 403-blocked from Pinnacle). iterations.ci_method: paired bootstrap, 300 reps, walk-forward OOS on 226 historical matches
iterations.honest_verdict: EM-fit lambda_3 collapsed to ~1e-5 (essentially independent Poisson) on this corpus, so the bivariate Poisson degenerates back to the baseline. Brier delta +0.0010 with CI [-0.0015, +0.0035] straddles 0. Goal-correlation common shock not material for international football where venues, opposition quality, and game-state dominate; can re-test if a different corpus shows materially correlated H/A scoring.

Brier delta -0.1383 strongly favours the RF+Poisson hybrid, BUT 95% CI [-0.343, +0.064] straddles 0 — wide because n=29 is small relative to the model's effective DoF (RF with 5 features at depth 10). Cannot adopt without OOS confirmation; re-evaluate after >= 60 graded fixtures.

iterations.ci_method: paired bootstrap on per-match hits, 300 reps, leave-one-out CV
iterations.honest_verdict: Stacked LR ensemble actually LOSES 2.9pp vs the single-best model (llama 57.1% > ensemble 50.0%) and 95% CI [-25.0pp, +21.4pp] straddles 0. With n=28 the stacker is over-parameterised relative to the data; revisit after >= 60 graded matches with held-out folds.

iterations.ci_method: paired bootstrap on per-match Brier deltas; reps=2000 (h-013..h-032), 300 (h-033), 5000 (h-034); percentile 2.5/97.5
iterations.scope: h-013..h-032 = top-20 30k-search hyperparameter points (re-scored on n=30 WC2026 verified actuals); h-033 = per-class isotonic on llama3.3:70b graded predictions (5-fold CV); h-034 = h-010 365d Heuer-decay Elo + h-012-style 5-fold isotonic-CV calibration.
iterations.honest_verdict: No statistically significant improvement on n=30 graded WC2026 matches. Under the corrected sign convention (brier_delta = candidate - baseline; negative = better; real_lift requires ci_95[1] < 0 strictly), every node h-013..h-034 either has a 95% paired-bootstrap CI that straddles zero (h-013..h-032 all have point estimates in the favourable direction [-0.060, -0.052] but upper CI bounds 0.060..0.073 sit above zero) or has a positive point estimate altogether (h-033: +0.087, h-034: +0.030 — calibration on top of 70B/Heuer365 makes Brier WORSE on this n). Production stays on h-001 (baseline Elo+log-linear-Poisson with Dixon-Coles low-score adjustment and the previously-adopted isotonic calibrator). Re-check after more matches play — when n_graded passes 60 (post-WC2026 group stage), rerun the top-20 search-point evaluation and h-034 calibration: the point estimates for h-013..h-032 are all in the favourable direction so a tighter CI on a larger sample may well exclude zero.
